Career Fair Oct. 13

The Career Fair is listed on Handshake and you can register to attend.

Humanities (English, History, Poli Sci, Languages, Philosophy, Religion) 

Art & Music

There are MANY Non-Profits where you can wear a lot of hats and learn how your major helps you – help people.

Oct. 13 – 11 am – 1 pm 

Graham Conf. Center 

Show up and Network!

Fellowship of Christian Athletes

YOU’RE INVITED! 
Join us for FCA tomorrow, 10/6 , in the BMW rooms at 8pm . Our leaders will be guiding us through discussions on sins we tolerate and what the Bible says about them. We hope to see you there! 

All Ministry Worship Night Next Week: 

Next Tuesday, 10/13 , FCA and the other ministries on campus will be putting on a Worship Night at 8pm around the fire pit near the pond . We would love to see you there to enjoy worship with other students and smores! 

Have a great week! 

- FCA Leadership Team

Men's & Women's Retreat/Getaway/Vacation! (Fall Break)

Calling all students! Want to get away for fall break? Stay in an awesome airbnb? Looking for some community? Join us for a weekend away, October 16-18, for tourist excursions, games, campfires, worship, GREAT food, coffee, Bible study, thrifting, & much more on the CM Men’s & Women's retreat. Both men are & women are headed to Des Moines. P.S. It is only $50! Email/talk to Hannah Goemaat in the lower chapel! Sign up here (spots limited): https://forms.gle/VqQqei6zqTEqZ3EE6

FALL BREAK TRIP TO CIVIL WAR BATTLEFIELDS IN TENNESSEE

You are invited to join History Club and Drs. Barloon and L.Witt over Fall Break to see the battlefields where most Iowa regiments fought in the Civil War over 160 years ago: Shiloh, Corinth, and Forts Henry & Donelson in Tennessee. Learn what happened, hike the battlefields, see the Fall colors! Cost of the trip is $240 for 3 nights lodging plus meal money. History Club will pay for one meal and the cost of travel. Leaving Friday, Oct. 16th at noon and returning Monday, October 19th. Let Drs. Barloon or L.Witt know if you want to go by Friday, October 9th.

In the Field with Harry Smith and Heather Lynch: Penguins of Antarctica

Heather Lynch, “NatGeo Live” host and associate professor of ecology and evolution at Stony Brook University, will speak on campus at 7 p.m. Tuesday, Oct. 6, in Douwstra Auditorium . 
Join Harry Smith, award-winning broadcast journalist, storyteller and 1973 graduate, and Lynch as she dives into her research tracking Antarctic wildlife, such as penguins, and how it helps scientists understand climate chang 

“Penguins are the canary in the coal mine that is this massive issue,” Smith says. “It’s a unique insight that anyone hoping for a better, healthier planet should hear.”
